tasks.short: Instruct people exploring conversion to a faith

steps.what: Instruct people seeking conversion, discuss beliefs and respond to their questions

tasks.design: Retain personal instruction and dialogue with the person exploring conversion. Existing teaching texts in {DOCS} may remain references; no automated persuasion, belief assessment or new documentation step is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on trust, voluntary exploration and the tradition's teaching practice.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed to replace this relationship.
tasks.still_hard: A person's questions and circumstances may not follow a standard course.
tasks.human_edge: Respect uncertainty and autonomy while explaining the faith honestly.
tasks.altitude: Instruction and pastoral responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Tradition-specific teaching and respectful responses to differing beliefs

evidence.claim: Faith instruction involves contextual dialogue and pastoral judgement; no time saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is clergy instruction, excluding learner study, registration and any formal rite. Learner effort is not in the denominator.

Seeker supplies questions voluntarily in s1 and clergy supplies teaching; all listening and explanation time remains. No new structured belief record or personal-data extraction is required. Unresolved doctrinal questions use existing human consultation.
Native reference access is considered first. Zero incremental upkeep because the instruction workflow is unchanged; no runtime earns labour savings.
research_questions: Which introductory materials support dialogue without replacing personal questions?

incremental.description: No added workflow or system upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and upkeep 0. Both straightforward and complex conversion instruction retain all clergy time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Share religious information through writing and teaching

steps.what: Study religious issues and compose the intended teaching or article content
Format authored content as an article, speech notes or teaching handout
Check the material and share it through publication, speech or teaching

tasks.design: Use native styles and reusable layouts in {DOCS} for clergy-authored material. The clergy member retains interpretation, original composition, final content checks and the actual speech, teaching or publication decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layout work across handouts, notes and articles.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse formatting without generating religious interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Meaning, pastoral sensitivity and authentic communication cannot be checked through layout rules.
tasks.human_edge: Connect a teaching to the community's concerns without misrepresenting the tradition.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting; authorship and public teaching remain personal responsibilities.

reach.task: Adapt an authored teaching into a usable handout
reach.learn: Accessible presentation without changing doctrinal meaning

evidence.claim: Native document templates can reduce repeated formatting while leaving religious authorship and teaching intact.

assumptions: Boundary includes clergy composition, formatting and sharing, excluding separate member mailings and event administration. Shares describe a recurring mix of articles, speeches and teaching, not three mandatory outputs per occasion.

Clergy produces authored text in s1 and selects format and audience in s2; its retained time includes layout choices and checks. Existing publication templates are maintained through the allowance below. Missing layouts use manual formatting in s2, never generated quotations or claims.
Test native styles first. No pastoral case details or member lists enter a new service. All study, composition and public interaction keep their time; runtime is not counted as labour.
unknowns: Publication approval rules and accessibility needs
research_questions: Do reusable layouts save time after checking that meaning and emphasis are preserved?

already_counted.description: Select format and review layout and emphasis

approvals.approved_version: Exact formatted text and intended publication or teaching context checked before sharing; changes require another check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=92; gross 8 minus upkeep 1 gives net 7. High assumes repeated layout work; low assumes bespoke formats consume gains. Study, authorship and sharing retain 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel people about spiritual and personal needs

steps.what: Counsel individuals or groups about spiritual, emotional or personal needs

tasks.design: Retain confidential pastoral counselling with a person. Existing referral guidance in {DOCS} remains a reference; the design adds no transcription, automated emotional assessment or generated personal advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The core work is attentive listening and situated pastoral judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed to replace confidential counselling.
tasks.still_hard: Risk, distress and the person's wishes need careful understanding and appropriate referral.
tasks.human_edge: Be present with distress while recognising the limits of pastoral support.
tasks.altitude: Counselling time and pastoral responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Receive an appropriate referral beyond pastoral competence
reach.learn: Referral boundaries, safeguarding and respectful consent

evidence.claim: Pastoral counselling needs personal listening and contextual judgement; this scenario claims no automation saving.
Religious affiliation can reveal special-category personal data under GDPR Article 9.

assumptions: Boundary is clergy counselling, excluding clinical treatment, referral-provider work and any separately required records.

Person supplies their account in s1 and clergy listens and responds with all time retained. No structured emotional score, transcript or belief profile is produced. Uncertainty or risk uses existing human safeguarding and referral procedures.
Native reference support is considered first. Zero incremental upkeep because no change is implemented; no outside labour or system runtime is credited as saving.
research_questions: Where do existing referral pathways fail to support people promptly?

incremental.description: Unchanged counselling workflow adds no upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and upkeep 0. Brief and complex pastoral conversations retain their time; no invented note-writing baseline is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Administer religious rites or ordinances according to the tradition and participants' circumstances

tasks.design: Keep the rite or ordinance with the authorised clergy member. Existing texts in {DOCS} may support the practice; no ritual action or spiritual eligibility decision is delegated to software.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is the religious act itself, carried out under the tradition's rules.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed to replace that act.
tasks.still_hard: Pastoral circumstances and tradition-specific requirements need human attention.
tasks.human_edge: Respond sensitively to the participants while preserving the meaning of the rite.
tasks.altitude: Religious authority and time spent administering rites stay unchanged.

reach.task: Support practical arrangements for a rite

evidence.claim: Administering a religious rite is a human and tradition-specific function; no labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is administration of the rite, excluding event bookings, member registration and preparation of certificates. Those tasks must not be folded into a fictitious administrative baseline here.

Clergy establishes relevant circumstances through existing practice within s1, with full time retained. No new structured eligibility input is required; uncertainty is resolved through the tradition's existing human authority.
Native reference access is considered first. Zero incremental upkeep because no workflow or system change is proposed; runtime earns no saving.
research_questions: Which practical arrangements belong to a separate coordinator workflow?

incremental.description: Unchanged rite administration adds no upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 with upkeep 0. Routine and unusual rites retain all clergy effort; no unsupported preparation saving is claimed.

role.altitude: Pastoral relationships, teaching and rites remain human; only repeated document formatting changes.
reach: Work with religious education colleagues and appropriate referral professionals
role.ambitious_version: Offer thoughtful pastoral care and clear religious teaching while retaining personal responsibility.
